held.why: REFUSED: Six sentences; the house form allows 3-5. Content is accurate (lines 1-2: 'sat down on / a stile which led thence into a field'), but the script must lose a sentence.

REFUSED: Never reaches the key. It says 'One made a request; another agreed to it. Read which way round it goes.' but never shows that line 14 gives 'at Lady Canterville's earnest request' and Mrs Otis 'had consented', so the child is not told which way round it goes, and that is the step that rules out the reversal distractor.

REFUSED: 'She says what she is afraid of' takes the polite idiom 'I am afraid something has been spilt' as fear, which misleads. The last sentence, 'What Mrs Umney says next is not yet hers.', is opaque to a 9-11-year-old: it does not say what Mrs Umney says or why that rules out option B.

REFUSED: Never shows the answer words. The script cites lines 16 and 18, then says only 'Then he names what it really is.' It does not point to 'It's the pudden' (line 18) or 'apricot roll-up' (line 19), and it does not connect 'pudden' to the key's 'pudding'. The closing sentence about the exclamation answers a question nobody asked.

REFUSED: 'Line 2 gives the reason he turned round' claims something the passage does not say, because Jim never turns round. It also skips the question's own anchor, 'I ran on deck.' on line 2, which is the sentence the apple explains.

REFUSED: 'Line 18 says that behind the peaceful and sunlit countryside there rose ever something.' The words 'there rose ever' are on line 19, not line 18. 'rose ever something' is also not English a 9-11-year-old reads easily.

REFUSED: 'Line 59 gives the old stone pillars on either side.' The passage never says the pillars are stone. Line 59 has 'weather-bitten pillars on either side, blotched with lichens'. That matters here because a distractor is 'A stone lamp'.

REFUSED: Never points to 'considered herself literary' (lines 7-8), the words the question asks about. It ties the sermons to 'took any talk of books as a challenge' instead. It also names the rector (distractor A) without ruling it out, and 'the strength she went on' is not easy English for a child.
REFUSED: 'The same line says he had it only that morning.' Line 20 ends 'I had it'. The words 'only this morning' are on line 21, so the citation is wrong.
